one_liner: Build an honest small-model eval harness, then quantize and serve the model on a laptop CPU.

key_terms.definition: Exponentiated average negative log-likelihood a model assigns to held-out text; here the single most trustworthy, ungameable eval number.
Converting a trained model's fp32/bf16 weights to low-bit integers after training completes, with no gradient updates required.
Baseline PTQ scheme: pick a per-group scale (and optional zero-point) from weight min/max, then round each weight independently to the nearest integer level.
Reconstruction-aware PTQ that quantizes a weight matrix column by column, using the layer's Hessian to push each column's rounding error onto not-yet-quantized columns.
PTQ method that rescales weight columns feeding high-activation-magnitude ('salient') channels before quantizing, protecting them from rounding error instead of correcting for it afterward.
Multiple-choice evaluation technique that ranks answer options by the model's summed log-probability of each full continuation, rather than asking it to emit a letter choice.
Stored per-layer key/value tensors from prior tokens, reused during autoregressive decoding so each new token attends without recomputing earlier positions.
Attention variant where several query heads share a smaller number of key/value heads, shrinking the KV cache relative to plain multi-head attention.
The failure mode where post-training (SFT/DPO/RLVR) quietly degrades a model's core language-modeling ability, detectable by comparing base vs. post-trained perplexity.
A quantization layout that assigns one shared scale (and zero-point) to each contiguous block of a fixed number of weights, trading finer granularity for more overhead as the group shrinks.

prerequisites: autoregressive decoding and the KV cache
